name: Ironbridge Gorge (The Iron Bridge)
description: The Iron Bridge opened in 1781, the first major bridge in the world made of cast iron. Upstream at Coalbrookdale, Abraham Darby I first smelted iron with coke in 1709.
image_credit: G K Raftery, via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 3.0)

name: Science and Industry Museum
description: Built on the site of Liverpool Road station, the Manchester terminus of the Liverpool and Manchester Railway, which opened on 15 September 1830.
image_credit: Science Museum Group, via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)

name: Quarry Bank Mill
description: A cotton mill built in 1784 by Samuel Greg at Styal, Cheshire, with housing for its workers and a working spinning mule.
image_credit: Francis Franklin, via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)

name: Big Pit National Coal Museum
description: A working coal mine from 1880 to 1980, opened to the public as a museum in 1983.
image_credit: Rafaël Delaedt (Arafi), via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 2.5)

name: Blaenavon (Blaenafon) Ironworks
description: Ironworks built after Midlands ironmasters took the lease in 1788-89; part of the Blaenavon Industrial Landscape World Heritage Site (2000).
image_credit: Alan Stanton, via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 2.0)

name: New Lanark
description: Cotton mills and a planned village opened by David Dale in 1786. Robert Owen became mill manager in 1800. The mills ran until 1968.
image_credit: user:R Pollack, via Wikimedia Commons (Public domain)
